newsitem.title: USA: Alliance Global plans to be open-end fund.
newsitem.headline: Alliance Global plans to be open-end fund.

text.p: Alliance Global Environment Fund Inc Wednesday its board has approved a plan to convert the company into an open-end fund.
The board is recommending stockholder approval of the conversion plan, the fund said.

As of April 18, the fund said its total net assets were about $97 million and net asset value per share was $16.24. The fund closed at $13.125 on the same day, representing a discount to net asset value of 19.2 percent.
The decision to convert to an open fund was made after results of the recent repurchase of about 13.6 percent or 939,900 shares of its common stock at $12.70 a share, or $11.9 million.

The fund, which is managed by Alliance Capital Management LP, said that while the repurchase was one of the largest for an American closed-end fund, the repurchase did not significantly affect its market discount.

"In view of the fund's exceptional recent performance record and our continuing conviction in the investment merit of the global environmental sector, we concluded, and the board of directors agreed, that it would be in the best interests of the fund and its stockholders for the fund" to become an open-end fund, said John Carifa, president of Alliance and chairman of the fund.
A closed-end fund has a limited number of shares outstanding, while an open-end fund creates new shares to meet investor demand.
